headline: Cabinet approves fiscal year change to April-March from FY 2028-29
summary: The government will shift the fiscal cycle to avoid monsoon rains that delay infrastructure projects and cause public suffering.
details: The government has decided to change the fiscal year cycle from July 1-June 30 to April 1-March 31, starting from the 2028-29 fiscal year.
The decision was approved during the 17th cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
To transition to the new timeline, the 2027-28 fiscal year will be a shortened transitional year, concluding in nine months from July to March.
The Cabinet Division explained that infrastructure development often continues during the July-August monsoon season, leading to rain-induced delays and compromised work quality.
By shifting the cycle to April-March, the government aims to ensure that infrastructure projects can be completed before the onset of the monsoon.
Additionally, the cabinet approved the draft of the 'Special Response Battalion (SRB) Act, 2026' and the 'National Strategy and Multi-Year Action Plan for a Lead-Free Bangladesh (2026-2035)'.
The meeting also approved a proposal to grant customs duty and tax exemptions on the import of green chillies and tomatoes.
caption:
Bangladesh is changing its fiscal year. Starting FY 2028-29, the cycle will move to April-March to beat the monsoon rains.

The government has decided to change the fiscal year cycle from July 1-June 30 to April 1-March 31, starting from the 2028-29 fiscal year.

The decision was approved during the 17th cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

To transition to the new timeline, the 2027-28 fiscal year will be a shortened transitional year, concluding in nine months from July to March.

The Cabinet Division explained that infrastructure development often continues during the July-August monsoon season, leading to rain-induced delays and compromised work quality.

By shifting the cycle to April-March, the government aims to ensure that infrastructure projects can be completed before the onset of the monsoon.

Additionally, the cabinet approved the draft of the 'Special Response Battalion (SRB) Act, 2026' and the 'National Strategy and Multi-Year Action Plan for a Lead-Free Bangladesh (2026-2035)'.

The meeting also approved a proposal to grant customs duty and tax exemptions on the import of green chillies and tomatoes.

headline_marked: Saudi Crown Prince [[invites Tarique Rahman to Saudi Arabia]] for talks
headline: Saudi Crown Prince invites Tarique Rahman to Saudi Arabia for talks
summary: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman seeks to strengthen bilateral relations and discuss regional and international issues with the Prime Minister.
details: Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud has invited Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to visit Saudi Arabia.
The invitation was delivered by Saudi Ambassador to Bangladesh Dr Abdullah Zafer H bin Abiyah during a meeting at the PM’s office in the Secretariat today.
In the letter, the Crown Prince expressed a keenness to further strengthen bilateral relations between the two nations in areas of mutual interest.
The visit aims to facilitate discussions on regional and international issues and fulfill the aspirations of the two countries and their people.
The date and schedule of the visit will be determined through diplomatic channels at a mutually convenient time.
Mohammed bin Salman also conveyed his wishes for Tarique Rahman’s health, happiness, and the continued prosperity of the people of Bangladesh.
caption:
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has officially invited Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to visit Saudi Arabia.

Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud has invited Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to visit Saudi Arabia.

The invitation was delivered by Saudi Ambassador to Bangladesh Dr Abdullah Zafer H bin Abiyah during a meeting at the PM’s office in the Secretariat today.

In the letter, the Crown Prince expressed a keenness to further strengthen bilateral relations between the two nations in areas of mutual interest.

The visit aims to facilitate discussions on regional and international issues and fulfill the aspirations of the two countries and their people.

The date and schedule of the visit will be determined through diplomatic channels at a mutually convenient time.

Mohammed bin Salman also conveyed his wishes for Tarique Rahman’s health, happiness, and the continued prosperity of the people of Bangladesh.
